label: r2c2
name: best + 2 epochs, more samples
hypothesis: Change: same network and n_envs 128 as r1c2, but ppo_epochs drops from 4 to 2. That nearly doubles the sample budget (about 234k steps, about 114 updates). Fresh random designs may be worth more than reusing old ones, and it also gives more updates. Refuted if dev success is at or below the 0.87 of r1c2 with 4 epochs, which would mean reusing samples matters more.
last_analysis: Mirroring the head along x fixed the starting architecture's 0.0 result. Seed-0 traces confirm that action x fills columns X-dx-x to X-1-x. On top of that head, recipe changes mattered most. Doubling updates (r1c2, 0.87) beat the default recipe (0.71). Two PPO epochs (r2c2, 0.927) beat four. The global-context head (r2c3, 0.913) is within noise of the best. The main risk is training collapse. Early random placements earn negative reward while DONE earns 0, so some seeds learn to end every episode at once: one r3c1 seed and both r3c3 seeds. One epoch instead fell into using only 1x1 bricks. More aggressive updates seem to raise this risk: one epoch, or minibatches of 1,024 samples with two epochs. A deeper trunk lost too many samples. For this last round I keep r2c2 and change one thing in each candidate: more entropy against collapse and ruts, a longer horizon for the exact-build bonus, or three epochs.
